levelNote: Foundational questions on Edwardian fiction, drama, poetry, ideas and Irish theatre.

questions.question: Who wrote the play Pygmalion?
questions.explanation: Shaw used the story of Eliza Doolittle to examine social class and the power of speech.

questions.question: Which Shaw play centers on a flower seller learning new speech habits?
questions.explanation: Eliza Doolittle receives phonetics lessons and discovers how accents shape social judgments.

questions.question: What institution features prominently in Shaw’s Major Barbara?
questions.explanation: Barbara works with the Salvation Army, and the play questions its relation to wealth and power.

questions.question: In what year did Shaw receive the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.explanation: Shaw won the literature prize in 1925, after becoming famous for his plays of ideas.

questions.question: Which Shaw play includes the philosophical episode Don Juan in Hell?
questions.explanation: The dream interlude in Man and Superman turns a comedy into a debate about life and evolution.

questions.question: Which family stands at the centre of The Man of Property?
questions.explanation: The novel introduces the prosperous Forsytes and their possessive ideas of family and property.

questions.question: Who wrote the 1906 novel The Man of Property?
questions.explanation: Galsworthy began his extended portrait of an English upper-middle-class family with this novel.

questions.question: What major international literary prize did Galsworthy win in 1932?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Prize recognised his literary achievements, especially his portrayal of the Forsytes.

questions.question: The Silver Box by John Galsworthy belongs to which literary genre?
questions.explanation: The Silver Box is a stage play that contrasts how rich and poor people are treated.

questions.question: In which year did Galsworthy publish The Man of Property?
questions.explanation: The Man of Property appeared in 1906 and became the first Forsyte novel.

questions.question: Which Bennett novel follows the divergent lives of two sisters?
questions.explanation: The story traces sisters Constance and Sophia from youth to old age in very different settings.

questions.question: Bennett’s fictional Five Towns are based mainly on which English district?
questions.explanation: The Five Towns fictionalise the pottery towns of Staffordshire where Bennett grew up.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Clayhanger?
questions.explanation: Clayhanger is part of Bennett’s fiction about provincial life in the Five Towns.

questions.question: Which Bennett novel, first published in 1902, takes its name from the Five Towns?
questions.explanation: The 1902 novel places Anna within Bennett’s fictional pottery-town community.

questions.question: Which novelist was the target of Virginia Woolf’s essay Mr Bennett and Mrs Brown?
questions.explanation: Woolf used Bennett to criticize fiction overly concerned with outward details rather than inner life.

questions.question: Who wrote Tono-Bungay, an Edwardian novel about commerce and society?
questions.explanation: Wells used the business world to expose pretensions and inequalities of Edwardian society.

questions.question: Which H. G. Wells novel about a young draper appeared in 1905?
questions.explanation: Kipps follows a shop assistant thrust into unfamiliar social circumstances.

questions.question: Which early Wells book is a classic of time-travel science fiction?
questions.explanation: The Time Machine imagines a journey into humanity’s distant future.

questions.question: Which novel by Wells portrays a young woman resisting conventional restrictions?
questions.explanation: Ann Veronica questions the limits imposed on a young woman’s freedom and choices.

questions.question: In what year was Wells’s social novel Tono-Bungay published?
questions.explanation: Tono-Bungay appeared in 1909 during Wells’s period of socially focused fiction.

questions.question: Which Conrad novel is set in the imaginary South American republic of Costaguana?
questions.explanation: Nostromo explores power, politics and conflicting loyalties in Costaguana.

questions.question: Which English-language novelist was born in Poland and had worked at sea?
questions.explanation: Conrad drew on his seafaring life and brought a distinctive international perspective to fiction.

questions.question: Which Conrad novel portrays anarchist intrigue in London?
questions.explanation: The Secret Agent depicts political conspiracy and violence in metropolitan life.

questions.question: Which Conrad novel focuses on a sailor seeking moral redemption after a failure?
questions.explanation: Jim’s struggle with dishonour and courage is central to the novel.

questions.question: English was Joseph Conrad’s language number what, after Polish and French?
questions.explanation: Polish was Conrad’s mother tongue, French was another early language, and he wrote fiction in English.

questions.question: Which E. M. Forster novel is named after an inherited country house?
questions.explanation: The house becomes a focus for questions of belonging, class and relationships.

questions.question: Which Forster novel published in 1908 takes place partly in Italy?
questions.explanation: A Room with a View contrasts the liberating experience of Italy with English convention.

questions.question: Which 1924 Forster novel examines tensions under British rule in India?
questions.explanation: A Passage to India dramatizes the difficulties of friendship under colonial power.

questions.question: Who wrote the critical study Aspects of the Novel?
questions.explanation: Forster’s lectures discuss story, plot, characters and other elements of fiction.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Forster’s fiction:
I. Forster wrote Howards End.
II. His novel A Room with a View appeared in 1908.
III. His first novel was A Passage to India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Howards End and A Room with a View are Forster novels; Where Angels Fear to Tread was his first published novel.

questions.question: Which Yeats poem imagines escaping to a quiet island retreat?
questions.explanation: The speaker dreams of a small cabin and the peace of an island in Lough Gill.

questions.question: Which Yeats poem responds to the Irish uprising of 1916?
questions.explanation: The poem reflects on the Easter Rising and the complicated transformation of its participants.

questions.question: Which poet was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923?
questions.explanation: Yeats received the prize in 1923 in recognition of his distinctive poetry.

questions.question: Yeats drew heavily on the legends and folklore of which country?
questions.explanation: Irish folklore and myth shaped his early imaginative world and work for the theatre.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding early Yeats:
I. He was primarily known as a naturalist novelist.
II. He helped foster the Irish literary revival.
III. His early work drew on Irish legend.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Yeats was a poet and dramatist who drew on Irish myth, not principally a naturalist novelist.

questions.question: Who wrote the epic verse drama The Dynasts?
questions.explanation: Hardy wrote the expansive dramatic work after returning his attention to poetry.

questions.question: Which historical wars are the central background of Hardy’s The Dynasts?
questions.explanation: The Dynasts spans the Napoleonic period while viewing human action on a grand scale.

questions.question: What was the title of Hardy’s verse collection issued in 1898?
questions.explanation: Wessex Poems marked Hardy’s public emergence as a major poet after his fiction career.

questions.question: After Jude the Obscure, which genre received Hardy’s main creative attention?
questions.explanation: After the controversial reception of his final major novel, Hardy concentrated on verse.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Hardy’s later career:
I. The Dynasts was issued in three parts.
II. Hardy abandoned verse to write new novels after 1900.
III. Hardy published Time’s Laughingstocks in 1909.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hardy issued The Dynasts in three parts and Time’s Laughingstocks in 1909, but wrote no further novels.

questions.question: Who wrote the one-act tragedy Riders to the Sea?
questions.explanation: Synge shaped the lives of an island fishing family into a short tragic drama.

questions.question: In what year did The Playboy of the Western World provoke riots?
questions.explanation: The play caused angry reactions during its Abbey Theatre performances in 1907.

questions.question: Which Irish islands inspired Synge’s rhythms of speech and dramatic settings?
questions.explanation: Synge travelled to the Aran Islands and drew on local storytelling and speech.

questions.question: What is the name of the mother in Riders to the Sea?
questions.explanation: Maurya fears the sea will take the remaining members of her family.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Synge’s plays:
I. Riders to the Sea is a one-act tragedy.
II. The Playboy of the Western World caused controversy.
III. Synge wrote The Importance of Being Earnest.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Synge wrote the two Irish plays, whereas the comedy in Statement III was written by Oscar Wilde.

questions.question: In which city did the Abbey Theatre open?
questions.explanation: The Abbey opened in Dublin to provide a stage for distinctly Irish theatrical work.

questions.question: In which year was the Abbey Theatre inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The theatre opened in December 1904 as a home for Irish plays.

questions.question: Which patron helped fund the early Abbey Theatre?
questions.explanation: Horniman’s support enabled the group to establish a permanent theatre in Dublin.

questions.question: Which Irish woman playwright helped Yeats found the Abbey Theatre?
questions.explanation: Lady Gregory worked with Yeats in establishing and sustaining the Abbey Theatre.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Abbey Theatre:
I. It opened during Queen Victoria’s reign.
II. Its programme promoted plays about Irish life.
III. The theatre was established in Dublin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Abbey opened in 1904, after Victoria’s death, and promoted Irish drama.
